newsitem.title: USA: Columbia says 270 mmcfd gas cut due storm.
newsitem.headline: Columbia says 270 mmcfd gas cut due storm.

text.p: Columbia Gulf Transmission, a unit of Columbia Gas System, said Friday about 270 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas has been cut from its system due to Hurricane Danny.

"As of this morning, we have a total of 270 million (cfd) cut. About 200 million is gas from a gas processing plant in Venice, Louisiana, which was shut last night. The rest of it is scattered shut ins in the Gulf where producers have shut in," a company spokesman said.
He said Columbia's offshore flows were roughly running at 750 mmcfd.
Danny was upgraded to a hurricane last night when sustained winds exceeded 74 mph.

At 0800 EDT, the storm was located at latitude 29.6 north, longitude 89.5 west, or about 45 miles southeast of New Orleans, drifting northeast at about five mph with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph.
Danny was on track to make landfall somewhere between Mississippi and the western Florida Panhandle.
